title: Whole Grain Pasta with Tomato Sauce and Seafood

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with tomato sauce and seafood is a dish that combines whole‑grain pasta, a flavorful tomato‑based sauce, and a variety of seafood (shrimp, mussels, calamari). Whole grain pasta retains more fiber and nutrients than refined white pasta, while the tomato sauce provides lycopene and vitamin C. Seafood adds high‑quality protein, omega‑3 fatty acids, and essential minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta contains roughly twice the fiber of regular refined pasta.
Tomatoes used in the sauce are rich in lycopene, which becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
Seafood such as mussels and shrimp are natural sources of vitamin B12, rare in plant foods.
The tradition of pairing pasta with seafood originates from Mediterranean cuisine, where both are staples.
Cooking whole grain pasta takes slightly longer, but it holds a firmer texture.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta provides dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion and blood‑sugar regulation.

items.title: Protein and omega‑3 source
items.content: Seafood contributes complete protein and omega‑3 fatty acids beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Lycopene and vitamin C
items.content: The tomato sauce supplies antioxidants that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Seafood adds zinc, iron, and selenium, important for immune function and metabolism.

items.title: Lower glycemic index
items.content: Whole grain pasta has a lower glycemic index than white pasta, aiding appetite control.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels, or calamari.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauces often contain added salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Food contaminants
items.content: Certain seafood can contain heavy metals; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Overeating
items.content: The dish can be calorie‑dense due to pasta and oil in the sauce; keep portions moderate.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the pasta al dente, then toss it with hot tomato sauce and sautéed seafood. Garnish with fresh parsley, basil, or grated Parmesan. Serve immediately while the sauce is warm.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Keep unused seafood separate, chilled, and consume within 24 hours. Dry whole grain pasta should be kept in a cool, dry place.
